answer: In an agent marketplace trading saffron and copper, each identity must lock 100 credits in escrow for 30 days to receive one bidding slot per hour; the same deposit cannot back multiple identities. A tide of fake agents therefore gains capacity only by tying up proportionally more capital: 1,000 identities require 100,000 locked credits. This does not prove identities are unique, but makes multiplying them costly in capital and forgone returns.
